## What composition looks like

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
```julia
ar2 = AR(;
  damp_priors = [
    truncated(Normal(0.2, 0.2), 0, 1),
    truncated(Normal(0.1, 0.05), 0, 1)],
  init_priors = [Normal(0, 0.2), Normal(0, 0.2)],
  ϵ_t = HierarchicalNormal(
    std_prior = HalfNormal(0.1)))

ma1 = MA(;
  θ_priors = [truncated(Normal(0.0, 0.2), -1, 1)],
  ϵ_t = HierarchicalNormal(
    std_prior = HalfNormal(0.1)))

arma21 = @set ar2.ϵ_t = ma1
arima211 = DiffLatentModel(
  arma21, Normal(0, 0.2); d = 1)
```
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
![](../figures/composable-arima.png){height="480px" fig-align="center"}

::: {.callout-note}
`@set` swaps the AR innovations for the MA process. `AR` was never
told that `MA` exists.
:::
:::
::::

## Rebuilding EpiNow2 by composing parts

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="44%"}
- Reuse the ARIMA(2,1,1) and the negative binomial observation model
  from the worked example, unchanged
- `broadcast_weekly` turns the daily latent process into piecewise
  constant weekly $R_t$
- Day-of-week ascertainment wraps the observation model
- Two `LatentDelay` wrappers add the incubation period and then the
  reporting delay
:::
::: {.column width="56%"}
![](../figures/composable-epinow2-model.png){width="100%"}

::: {.callout-important}
Nothing here required editing a component that already existed. The new
code was the layers, not the model.
:::
:::
::::

## And it works

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="38%"}
- **A** and **B** check the weekly $R_t$ process and the latent
  infections on their own, before anything is composed
- **C** and **D** check the day-of-week effect and the two delay
  distributions the same way
- **E** and **F** are the joint fit. Cases are recovered through the
  delays, and $R_t$ with them
- The parts were validated separately and the composition was fitted
  together. That is the whole claim

::: {.attribution}
Replicating
[EpiNow2](https://doi.org/10.12688/wellcomeopenres.16006.2)
(Abbott et al., 2020). Figure from the paper.
:::
